paragraphs.text: The altar of burn offering, with its furniture Exo 38:1-7, laver of brass, Exo 38:8. The court, and the hangings thereof, Exo 38:9-20. Bezaleel and Aholiab make all ready, Exo 38:22,23. The sums of what the people offered, Exo 38:24-31.

as now they are sometimes made of polished steel, so anciently were made of polished brass, as appears both from sacred and from profane writers. See Job 37:18 Php 3:9, &c. The words following seem to note a company of religious women, who in a more peculiar manner devoted themselves to the service of God in or about his tabernacle, by fasting, prayer, &c. See 1Sa 2:22 Luk 2:37. And whereas some object that the tabernacle was not yet built, it may be replied, either that this is to be understood of the tabernacle spoken of Exo 33:7, which might serve for that purpose till this was built; or that here is a prolepsis or anticipation, and that he speaks not of what the women now did, but of what they did after the tabernacle was built, which was before Moses writ these words.

This doth not belong to the following account of gold and silver, but to the foregoing particulars of holy things relating to the tabernacle, for these only were committed to the care of the Levites, as it here follows, but this gold and silver was put into other hands.
i.e. for those holy uses and services which the Levites administered.
paragraphs.anchor: For the service of the Levites

paragraphs.text: Every talent contained three thousand shekels. See Gen 23:15 Exo 30:13. It is not said that all this gold and following silver were used about the building of the tabernacle, for the people brought much more than enough, Exo 36:5. And these remains, it is probable, were put into the sacred treasury, to be used as occasion should require.
